item.title: On Easter, Pope Leo delivers commanding message of peace to a world at war
item.summary: “Let those who have weapons lay them down!” the first American pope declared. The White House’s war in Iran and nativist agenda at home are testing the Vatican.

item.title: American universities in Middle East brace for Iranian retaliation
item.summary: After the U.S.-Israeli campaign struck Iranian universities, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps called American schools in the Middle East “legitimate targets.”

item.title: Chinese firms market Iran war intelligence ‘exposing’ U.S. forces
item.summary: Private Chinese technology companies — some with ties to the military — are marketing detailed intelligence on movements of U.S. forces in Iran, even as Beijing seeks to keep its distance.

item.title: It’s Holy Week, but Jerusalem’s Old City is quiet and eerily empty
item.summary: The Austrian Hospice urges groups of Christian pilgrims to book 16 months ahead. One night this week, a receptionist warned a Post reporter she would be the only guest.

item.title: Trump threatens Iran with ‘Hell’ over Strait of Hormuz in profane post
item.summary: Trump escalated threats against Iran’s power plants, bridges and other infrastructure in an expletive-laden post on Truth Social on Easter morning.

item.title: In Hungarian election, Trump and Putin are backing Viktor Orban
item.summary: Viktor Orban, who has built strong ties to the MAGA movement and the Kremlin, faces a tough electoral challenge from center-right candidate Peter Magyar on April 12.

item.title: Epstein victims demand meeting with King Charles in Washington
item.summary: A state visit intended to mark 250 years of U.S. independence could become a test of the British monarchy’s willingness to confront one of its most difficult controversies.
